scope: Database-grounded current canonical revisions and active catalog nodes. Counts deduplicate by revision UUID and exclude learner-created questions from canonical-bank coverage.

points.statement: Can explain cache hit, miss, load, and populate steps.
Can explain acknowledgement timing and redelivery.
Can explain coordination across service instances.
Can compare burst capacity and sustained rate.
Can design a safe repeated operation.

topics.name: HTTP
topics.description: HTTP semantics, caching, and transport behavior.

points.statement: Can distinguish freshness from validation.
Can explain method, status, headers, and body roles.

topics.name: TCP Reliability
topics.description: Explain ordered delivery, retransmission, and connection state without assuming application messages.

points.statement: Can explain how sequence numbers and retransmission recover missing bytes while preserving ordered delivery.
Can explain that TCP exposes a byte stream and does not preserve application write or message boundaries.

topics.name: Indexes
topics.description: Query access paths and index tradeoffs.

points.statement: Can explain how a composite B-tree index column order affects equality and range predicates.
Can weigh index selectivity and read benefit against write, storage, and maintenance cost.
Can describe atomic commit and isolation tradeoffs.
Can predict a non-repeatable read or serialization anomaly from a transaction schedule and isolation level.

topics.name: Arrays and Hashing
topics.description: Compare sequential storage with keyed lookup for concrete workloads.

points.statement: Can choose between array scanning and hash lookup from operation mix and expected complexity.
Can explain collision handling, key equality, and expected-versus-worst-case hash lookup.

topics.name: Trees and Graphs
topics.description: Choose traversal and search strategies from structure and requirements.

points.statement: Can choose BFS or DFS to satisfy shortest unweighted path, reachability, or traversal requirements.
Can explain when a visited set is required and bound traversal work by vertices and edges.

topics.name: Processes and Scheduling
topics.description: Explain process and thread state and how scheduling affects progress.

points.statement: Can distinguish process isolation from threads sharing an address space and resources.
Can explain how preemption and scheduling policy affect latency, fairness, and throughput.

topics.name: Synchronization
topics.description: Diagnose races and deadlocks and choose synchronization conditions.

points.statement: Can identify a data race and state the synchronization needed to protect an invariant.
Can diagnose deadlock using the four necessary conditions and propose a condition-breaking remedy.
Can estimate request rate and storage from explicit workload assumptions and unit conversions.
Can distinguish strong read-after-write behavior from eventual convergence for replicated data.
Can explain which consistency and availability behavior a client observes during a network partition.
Can choose a bounded fallback when a dependency fails and state which user-visible guarantee changes.
Can justify a boundary using scale and failure reasoning.
